# Pack: dbc-car-intel

CAN frames described by the DBC file `car_intel` of `https://github.com/commaai/opendbc` at commit `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`.
Source: `opendbc/dbc/car_intel.dbc`.
Public. Generated by `tools/gen/dbc2pack.py`; do not edit `pack.def`, this file,
`PROVENANCE.md`, `model/dbccarintel.def` or the vectors by hand.

Status: Built. Generated and checked by the generator's own serializer and codec.

## The message

One Linux SocketCAN `struct can_frame` (Linux UAPI header include/uapi/linux/can.h, struct can_frame (GPL-2.0 WITH Linux-syscall-note)),
as 16 bytes in hex text:

| Bytes | Content | In the pack |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | CAN identifier, little-endian; bit 31 extended frame, bit 30 remote request, bit 29 error frame | per-kind `when` on the whole word |
| 4 | data length in bytes | per-kind `when` = the DBC message size |
| 5-7 | padding | not mapped |
| 8-15 | data | the kind's `field` lines; a byte no signal uses in the last place is a `const 0` |

The frame carries its identifier, so a kind is chosen by `when` on it. A DBC
writes an extended identifier with bit 31 set, as SocketCAN does; an identifier
above 0x7FF without it is taken as a 29-bit identifier (opendbc writes some that
way) and the `when` holds it with bit 31 set. A data frame has bits 30 and 29
clear, so a remote or error frame matches no kind.

## Signals

The file has 20 Intel and 3 Motorola signals; the pack's bit order is `lsb`.
A signal's DBC start bit numbers bit `b` as bit `b mod 8` of data byte `b div 8`.
An Intel signal from start bit `s` is the field `0:64+s:<length>`. A Motorola
signal is a field when it lies in one byte, or covers whole bytes from a byte
boundary (`swap`); otherwise it is not mapped.

| DBC | Pack line | Model type |
|---|---|---|
| unsigned, factor 1, offset 0 | `uint` | int |
| signed, factor 1, offset 0 | `twos` | int |
| other factor or offset | `uscale` / `sscale` with the factor as an exact fraction | float |
| `SIG_VALTYPE_` 1 / 2 (IEEE float / double) | `f32` / `f64` | float |
| a `VAL_` table that names every raw value of an unscaled signal of up to 8 bits | the integer transform with `via` | string |
| a multiplexor (`M`) and its multiplexed signals (`m<n>`, or the values `SG_MUL_VAL_` lists for them) | one kind per value, a `when` on the multiplexor | - |

Keys are `dbccarintel.<message>_<signal>` in lower case, in the unit the DBC states.

| | Count |
|---|---|
| messages in the file | 9 |
| kinds | 7 |
| `field` lines | 17 |
| value tables applied | 2 |
| messages with no kind | 3 |
| signals not mapped | 4 |
| vectors | 8 |

### Core keys

A signal is bound to core `lat` / `lon` when its name ends in latitude or
longitude and the DBC states its unit as degrees, and its message has both:

- `GPS.GPS_latitude` (0|28@1, factor 1E-06, unit `deg`) to `lat`
- `GPS.GPS_longitude` (28|29@1, factor 1E-06, unit `deg`) to `lon`

### `requires`

Each kind requires up to 3 of its own keys, those the fewest kinds map, so an
entity from another format selects a kind only when it holds them.

## What is not mapped

Messages with no kind:

| Message | Identifier | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| FD_FRAME | 1536 | CAN FD: 64 data bytes (struct canfd_frame) |
| EMPTY | 700 | the message defines no signal |
| VECTOR__INDEPENDENT_SIG_MSG | 3221225472 | not a frame (identifier 0xc0000000) |

Signals not mapped:

| Message | Signal | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| SPEED | BIG_ENDIAN_ODD | Motorola signal over byte boundaries in an Intel (lsb) pack |
| SPEED | OVERLAP | overlaps another signal of the message |
| EXTENDED | Flag | outside the 4 data bytes |
| FLOATS | SCALED_FLOAT | float signal with a factor or an offset |

1 `VAL_` tables are not applied (they do not name every raw value, or the
signal is scaled or wider than 8 bits): those signals carry the number.

- Remote and error frames, and CAN FD frames (`struct canfd_frame`, up to 64 data bytes).
- Comments, attributes (`BA_`), node lists, signal value ranges and receivers.
- Extended multiplexing: more than one multiplexor in a message, or a multiplexor
  that is itself multiplexed.

## Vectors

`vectors/rt-NNNN-<kind>.json`: one same-format round trip per kind. The frame is
written by a DBC serializer in the generator from sample raw values (Intel
signals from the start bit upward; Motorola signals from the start bit as the
most significant bit, through the DBC bit numbering); expect equals input.

`vectors/x-01-…-to-geojson.json`: a frame whose latitude and longitude give
47.397742 and 8.545594 degrees, converted to GeoJSON; the expected text is
written by hand.
